events.title: Root & Wind
events.subtitle: 5-day Intensive Bari Kim
events.summary: Root & Wind explores the relationship between rooting and flying, stability and freedom, presence and movement.
events.teacher_bio:
Bari Kim is a dance artist, improviser, choreographer based in Jeju, Seoul in Korea and travels various places. She is performing/creating in a state of improvisation, dance of presence, exploring the vitality of time and space, the relationship between dance and music, the transparent body, modernity based on traditionality, movement as embodied nature. Her focus of dance is listening.

She believes that through listening, dance becomes dance itself, music becomes music itself which allows all the possibilities for the very moments arises, resonates and expresses. And poems in the space started to be written and read.

Her artistic theme/root is Poong-gyung and GAMU which is Every being dances and sings by itself. She keeps learning dance and music from the nature, East Asian philosphy, Buddhism philosophy and Korean traditional medical research.

She has been actively sharing her dance in various ways and performing solo, as well as collaborating with various dancers and musicians across different spaces in Korea, Europe and Asia such as Germany, Sweden, Denmark, Portugal, Czech Republic, Spain, Norway, Hungary, Taiwan, Thailand, Singapore, India, China, Japan, Ireland, Poland and Canada, etc. She had founded the improvisational performance group in 2008, experimenting with genre fusion and improvisation. also she has been working as a member of the groups- interdisciplinary duo, experimental music duo, and improvisation music/dance band.

She is also performing as a musician, a.k.a.CrystalEar, especially with her voice. She has participated in various international residencies, including Research into the Unknown, and has toured with various projects. She received Best Dance award 2020 from Korean dance critics association.

For 26 years, She has been experimenting, enjoying, learning from, growing with/by, living and performing improvisation dance. Contact improvisation is one of her passion and love. She teaches Contact improvisation in various places/intensive workshops and festivals-Seoul international improvisation dance festival, AIAE(Asia improvisation art exchange), Towards (Thailand contact improvisation conference), Samdal contact festival, Seoul Contact festival, AOI(Goa, India), Portugal New year festival, Italy contact festival, Water&Land festival, Ladoga festival, etc She studied French literature(B.A.) in Konkuk Univ. and choreography(M.F.A.) in Korean National University of Arts. She is also certified somatic movement educator(SME) of Body-Mind Centering®️(BMC) and completed Practitioner courses of BMC being in the process of graduation.

She studied with beautiful dance-movement artist/teachers, Nancy Stark Smith, Mike Vargas, Kurt Koegel, Katie Duck, Thomas Kampe, Ted stoffer, Gizegorz ziolkowisky, Sinja Hong, Jeongho Nam, Heekyung Blanz Kim, Eunsuk Jo, Joerg Hassmann, Stephanie Maher, Peter Pleyer, Eszter Gal, Jess Curtis, Keith Hennesy, Andrew Morrish, Rosalind Crisp, Daniel lepkoff, Julyen Hamilton, Lisa Nelson, Nina Martin, Walburga Glatz, Maryska Bigos, Bob Lehnberg, Jens Johannsen, Friederike Troscher, Bonnie Bainbridge Cohen.

www.instagram.com/bari.dance www.facebook.com/bari.kim www.youtube.com/@barikim0676

events.title: Deep Touch
events.subtitle: 3-Day Workshop with Rosalind Holgate-Smith
events.summary: On what it means to touch, and be touched deeply.
events.teacher_bio:
Rosalind Holgate Smith (UK) is a Dance Artist and Somatic Educator who creates performances and installations that explore intimate connections between people, place and the environment. She specialises in teaching Contact Improvisation and Contemporary Release Techniques and takes inspiration from Body Mind CenteringⓇ, Authentic Movement, Skinner Release Technique, Martial Arts and her love for dancing outdoors. She has PhD on the Vocabulary of Touch and encountering Otherness in Contact Improvisation and is currently a Dance Lecturer for Middlesex and Minzu University, on Hainan Island in China. Besides working in academia Rosalind has also taught dance for diverse communities, including children, disabled adults and older people. She is additionally an experienced Yoga Instructor and following her passion for water, she teaches swimming with the Shaw Method, which integrates the Alexander technique.

https://rosalindholgate-smith.com

events.title: To Be Danced By Spaces
events.subtitle: 3-Day Workshop with Nitipat Ong Pholchai
events.summary: Where do our bodies end and spaces begin? How might we surrender to being danced by the spaces we inhabit rather than merely dancing within them?
events.teacher_bio: Nitipat "Ong" Pholchai is a Thai interdisciplinary artist, educator and Contact Improvisation practitioner now based in Chiang Mai. Trained in physics at Harvard and Berkeley, he began dancing in the SF Bay area as a serious hobbies before returning to Thailand, where CI became a way of navigating uncertainty — political, economic, social — through the body. His work has unfolded alongside a blind artist seeking accessible space, a queer activist community, and a Buddhist sangha, shaping a practice he describes as quantum relational: an active, cellular-level listening between self and space. Ong is the founder of Conscious Movement Collective Bangkok and teaches, performs, and facilitates workshops exploring the body as a site of potentiality — where movement becomes both survival strategy and collective dreaming toward more liberated futures. He has had both the honor and the pleasure of meeting and exchanging embodied practice with practitioners and cultural communities around the world.

events.title: The Body Orchestra
events.subtitle: Axis Syllabus - Somatics - CI with Kira Kirsch
events.summary: 𝗔 𝗧𝘄𝗼-𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀𝗵𝗼𝗽 𝗶𝗻 𝗦𝗼𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗥𝗲𝗼𝗿𝗴𝗮𝗻𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝗕𝗶𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗟𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘆 & 𝗥𝗲𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗗𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗣𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗲
events.teacher_bio:
Kira Kirsch is a movement artist, community organizer, and experiential researcher, originally from East Berlin. After spending seven years in San Francisco, she now resides in Berlin with her family as residents of Lake Studios —a vibrant, artist-run space for dance, performance, and creative production. Kira is deeply invested into creating and shaping spaces for people to experience, learn about and sensitize their mind-body-movement continuum. She has pioneered, taught and continuously researched through the lens of the Axis Syllabus (AS) for more than 20 years and has established dance research communities in Brussels, San Francisco and Berlin.

Her work is deeply informed by studies in Moving Alchemy with Sarah Shelton Mann, Biodynamic Craniosacral Therapy, Mind in Motion with Nita Little, Nonviolent Communication (NVC), and Body-Mind Centering (BMC). As a curator, Kira has been involved with projects like the "SENSING IN" festival, mov*ed—a peer exchange platform for movement educators—and leads the Movement Artisans educational program in Berlin.

Kira’s teaching spans internationally, from contemporary dance festivals to contact improvisation gatherings, and she is a regular presence in professional dance institutions. Recent artistic collaborations include Many Lives with choreographer Jorge de Hoyos, (dis)comfort behaviours with actress Anneke Schwabe, Earth Will Come with filmmaker Katelyn Stiles and musician/poet Barnaby Tree, as well as the music video We Are the Flood and the short film Dreamstroy with the collective Cargocult.

events.title: Oneness Nowness
events.subtitle: From Nature to Studio with Yasukichi Suzuki
events.summary: "We receive boundless energy and gifts from Earth and nature.
events.teacher_bio:
One of the early disseminator of Contact Improvisation (CI) in Japan

26 years of CI practice with a warm heart

Active both in Japan and sometimes abroad,

Guest at CI festivals in Malaysia, Thailand, India,China.

CI dancer, contact improviser, CI jam maker , CI in water lover, and human.

She began leading regular CI jams in Tokyo around 2000 and started facilitating workshops in 2002, all while continuing to practice CI. She enjoys organizing & facilitating a variety of jams & workshops—both indoors and outdoors, on regular and irregular schedules—her workshops open to everyone, regardless of age or gender, including children, the elderly, and individuals with special needs. For her, 踊る事＝生 dancing is synonymous with “living”—with "love and peace.”愛と平和 and natural 自然

Based in Tokyo, she also travels abroad when invited. She has been happily practicing CI in water for nearly two decades and is a certified Watsu provider. Her solo improvisational performance works include the "Creatures of the Watery Sea" series, "Carrying Water...", and "Iro-Iro" etc.

Yasukichi Trained in studying with CI masters such as Daniel Lepkoff, Ray Chung, Martin Keogh, Joerg Hassman,Nina Martin, Karl Frost, Nancy Stark Smith, Steve Paxton, etc. and from many participants and from her daily life and nature.

events.title: Listening to Movement
events.subtitle: 5-Day Intensive with Antoine Ragot
events.teacher_bio:
Antoine Ragot is a Berlin-based dance artist and educator whose teaching draws deeply from the Axis Syllabus, of which he is a certifying teacher, and from a lifelong practice of Contact Improvisation.

With nearly two decades of experience, he is known as an insightful and approachable pedagogue and passionate movement researcher.

He co-founded Movement Artisans in Berlin, leads research-oriented intensives, and teaches across Europe. Antoine also co-produces other grassroots dance events close to his heart such as the New Year CI Festival and the Summer CI gathering in Basel as well as the SuperJam in Berlin.

His work emphasizes the simple joy of dancing together, biomechanics, functional morphology and athletic skills as well as the intersection of Contact Improvisation with proprioceptive communication.

events.title: Katya Basalaeva
events.subtitle: 5-Day Intensive & 3-Day Lab with Katya Basalaeva
events.summary: What does it mean to be in one place… in one moment… in one action?
events.teacher_bio:
Katya on herself and her practice: “I have been practicing and teaching CI since 2000 because I love this practice, and over time it keeps opening into new layers and possibilities.

Right now, I can describe my interest in Contact Improvisation roughly like this: Contact – as coherence, wholeness, inner consistency of the whole system involved in action. Improvisation – as the ability to create and shape forms, flows of forces, space, and time.

I like it when CI stays an exploration and a creation and does not shrink to learning and repeating familiar forms. What if we look not only at what has already been and what is, but also at what could be?

From the endless range of what is possible, what do I want to see manifested right now? What do I choose to embody, support, and sustain? What do I want, and what do I actually do? How do I want things to be? How do I want to bring order to chaos?

And what do we do with the accumulated baggage of patterns, ideas, and beliefs when they no longer serve the new tasks and challenges at hand?

I will be happy to welcome anyone who is ready to enter this experience—not of searching for themselves or for the dance, but of creating both.”
